DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY

U.S. Energy Information Administration

Agency Information Collection Proposed New Survey

AGENCY: U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), Department of 
Energy (DOE).

ACTION: Notice and request for comments.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY: EIA invites public comment on the proposed collection of 
information, Data Center Energy Consumption Survey (DCECS), as required 
under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995. Form EIA-872 will collect 
facility-level data on energy consumption and energy-related physical 
and operational characteristics from all U.S. data centers with a 
design capacity of at least 1 megawatt (MW). DCECS will be used to 
produce national statistics on data center energy consumption and 
electricity demand.

DATES: EIA must receive all comments on this proposed information 
collection no later than January 26, 2027. If you anticipate any 
difficulties in submitting your comments by the deadline, contact the 
person listed in the ADDRESSES section of this notice as soon as 
possible.

ADDRESSES: You may submit comments, identified by EIA-872: Data Center 
Energy Consumption Survey, by email to 
[email protected]
. Include 
the OMB control number listed in the subject line of the message.

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: Maura Bardos Chihil, EIA Clearance 
Officer, at (202) 586-7865, 
[email protected]
. The forms and 
instructions are available on EIA's website at 
www.eia.gov/survey/
.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: This information collection request 
contains:
    (1) OMB No.: New;
    (2) Information Collection Request Title: Data Center Energy 
Consumption Survey (DCECS);
    (3) Type of Request: New;
    (4) Purpose: Form EIA-872, Data Center Energy Consumption Survey 
(DCECS), will collect facility-level statistical information on energy 
consumption and energy-related physical and operational characteristics 
of data centers in the United States.
    Data centers exhibit high power densities when compared with other 
commercial spaces that would traditionally fall under EIA's Commercial 
Building Energy Consumption Survey (CBECS), which most recently 
collected data from 2018. A new survey is required because there are 
currently no sources that comprehensively measure end-use energy 
consumption of data centers and certain aspects of their operating 
profiles, which are driven by continuous information-technology (IT) 
loads, uninterruptible power supplies, complex liquid- and air-cooling 
systems, and other characteristics.
    For the purposes of this collection, a data center facility is 
defined as follows: ``A data center facility is comprised of a 
dedicated building, buildings, or a clearly delineated or partitioned 
portion of a building with the primary purpose of housing computer 
servers and associated IT equipment (e.g., storage, networking) and 
essential supporting infrastructure, including, but not limited to, 
uninterruptible power delivery, cooling systems, and network 
connectivity.
    A data center facility may be a campus, which is a multi-building 
complex where energy, cooling, or power delivery infrastructure is 
functionally integrated or shared across the buildings.''
    EIA will collect data annually for the previous reference year. EIA 
will send each company with at least one data center a questionnaire to 
identify a roster of data center facilities and will ask the company to 
provide data for each in-scope facility that has an IT design capacity 
of at least 1 MW. Facilities that meet the definition and capacity 
threshold may include enterprise data centers, colocation facilities, 
hyperscale facilities, edge data centers, super intelligence (SI) data 
centers, carrier hotels, network gateways, and cryptocurrency mines, 
but such facilities that do not meet the definition and capacity 
threshold will be excluded from DCECS reporting. EIA is not proposing 
to collect any confidential business information pertaining to the 
customers these facilities may serve.
    As part of the agency's effort to accelerate all consumption survey 
programs from a multi-year to an annual publication frequency, EIA will 
be conducting DCECS in 2027 as the annual data collection component of 
commercial energy consumption statistics.
    (5) Annual Estimated Number of Respondents: 1,400;
    (6) Annual Estimated Number of Total Responses: 1,400;
    (7) Annual Estimated Number of Burden Hours: 12,200;
    (8) Annual Estimated Reporting and Recordkeeping Cost Burden: The 
cost of the burden hours is estimated to be $1,158,268 (12,200 burden 
hours times $94.94 per hour).
    Comments are invited on whether or not: (a) The proposed collection 
of information is necessary for the proper performance of agency 
functions, including whether the information will have a practical 
utility; (b) EIA's estimate of the burden of the proposed collection of 
information, including the validity of the methodology and assumptions 
used, is accurate; (c) EIA can improve the quality, utility, and 
clarity of the information it will collect; (d) EIA can minimize the 
burden of the collection of information on respondents, such as 
automated collection techniques or other forms of information 
technology; and (e) EIA's definition of a data center facility to 
ensure that it is comprehensive and accurate.
    The information provided on Form EIA-872 will be used for 
statistical purposes only and is confidential by law. In accordance 
with the Confidential Information Protection and Statistical Efficiency 
Act of 2018 (44 U.S.C. 3572), responses will not be disclosed in 
identifiable form without consent. Collected data will be published 
only in aggregate form.
    Statutory Authority: 15 U.S.C. 772(b) and 42 U.S.C. 7101 et seq.
